chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who entered into Ihram in one month and freed from it in another, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is recorded for him according to what he intended, or it is recorded for him according to the superior of the two.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Freed from Ihram (ended the state of consecration)
key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for pilgrimage or Umrah)
key_terms.أَفْضَلِهِمَا: The superior of the two (referring to the months)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who enters Ihram in one month and ends it in another?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle of 'Ikhtiyar' (choice) in ritual rewards, where the Imam (peace be upon him) offers two valid options: recording the reward according to the pilgrim's specific intention or attributing it to the month deemed superior by scholarly consensus. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of divine law to accommodate the worshipper's intent while maintaining objective spiritual merit. It underscores the role of the Imam as the interpreter of the Quran's practical application in matters of worship.
